title: One-degree extension of a finite split basis hypercover truncation
statement: Let C be a category with pullbacks, with possibly distinct object and morphism universes, J any precoverage [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology], and B a set of objects. Formal-family index types lie in the maximum of those universes. Assume every object has a finite covering family from B, and adjoining any single arrow from a B-object to any finite B-cover again gives a cover, including empty covers. Fix T and n>=0. Let K be an n-truncated simplicial object [def-weil-pbc-simplicial-object] in formal families over T [def-weil-pbc-formal-coproduct], split in the explicit normalized-degeneracy sense of [lem-weil-pbc-site-hypercover-finite-extension]. Suppose every retained term has finite indices and B-components, and for each retained degree q its proper-face diagram [lem-weil-pbc-matching-object-proper-faces] has a limiting cone M_q and an arrow from K_q with the canonical projection equations and componentwise covering presieves. Require the degree-zero cone point to equal the singleton id_T. Then there exists a split (n+1)-truncation L restricting exactly to K, with all these same finite-basis and normalized matching-cover properties in every degree through n+1. No coherent choice of matching cones between degrees or stages is assumed.

proof.text: In D=C/T, obtain finite limits from the terminal object id_T and pullbacks. Let the boundary index category be CostructuredArrow(Delta_le_n -> Delta, [n+1]); its objects are all operators [r]->[n+1] with r<=n. Embed its object type into the finite disjoint union of these finite hom sets, and its hom sets into the hom sets of Delta. It is a finite category. The boundary diagram evaluates K at the source of each operator.

The index-set functor SR(D)->Type sends the terminal singleton family to PUnit and the componentwise pullback family to the ordinary pullback of index functions. Mathlib supplies the corresponding limiting cones, so this functor preserves terminal objects and pullbacks, hence finite limits. Take the actual limit of the finite boundary diagram in SR(D). Its index type is equivalent to the compatible sections of the finite diagram of finite index types, hence finite. Translate its cone into the BoundaryCone interface and its universal property into IsMatching.

For every matching component W_h choose the finite B-cover given by hcover. The sigma family V indexed by pairs (h,i) is finite and consists of basis objects over T. Its map v to M has index function (h,i)->h and components the chosen covering arrows over T. Each fibre presieve is exactly the chosen cover. Apply the existing split attachment theorem to K, M, V and v. It gives L with exact restriction K, the new term equality to V plus normalized degeneracies, finite indices, splitness, and the boundary projection equations.

Old components belong to B by the restriction equality. In the new term, the disjoint-sum description shows that components come either from V or from old terms, so all belong to B. For a fibre of the new matching map, the selected V-cover is a subpresieve of its finite family of arrows. Prove that any finite B-family containing a finite B-cover also covers: start with the cover, induct over a finite set of added arrows using hadjoin, then identify the final union with the desired presieve. This argument also treats empty chosen covers, and an empty matching index type leaves no condition.

Include the proper injective faces of [n+1] into the full boundary index category. This inclusion is final: for any full operator alpha, factor it through its injective image. The image has degree at most that of alpha and therefore at most n. Its factorization is an initial object of the structured-arrow category of factorizations of alpha through proper faces. The image universal property constructs the unique arrow to any other factorization; monicity proves uniqueness. The opposite inclusion is initial, so restricting the full limiting boundary cone gives a limiting proper-face cone with the same point. The attachment projection equations restrict to the required proper-face equations.

Transport each earlier matching cone, arrow, projection equation and covering condition along the exact restriction equality. Only the new top-degree condition uses the restricted boundary cone just constructed; its degree cannot be zero. Thus the prescribed degree-zero point is retained and every clause of IsFiniteBasisTruncation holds for L.

lean.statement:
theorem exists_finite_basis_truncation_extension
    {C : Type u} [Category.{v} C] [HasPullbacks C]
    (J : Precoverage C)
    (B : Set C)
    (hcover : ∀ T : C, ∃ (I : Type (max u v)) (U : I → C) (f : ∀ i : I, U i ⟶ T),
      Finite I ∧ (∀ i : I, U i ∈ B) ∧ Presieve.ofArrows U f ∈ J T)
    (hadjoin : ∀ (T : C) (I : Type (max u v)) [Finite I] (U : I → C)
      (f : ∀ i : I, U i ⟶ T), (∀ i : I, U i ∈ B) →
      Presieve.ofArrows U f ∈ J T → ∀ (V : C), V ∈ B → ∀ (g : V ⟶ T),
        Presieve.ofArrows U f ⊔ Presieve.singleton g ∈ J T)
    (T : C) (n : ℕ)
    (K : SimplicialObject.Truncated (FormalCoproduct.{max u v} (Over T)) n)
    (hK : IsFiniteBasisTruncation J B T K) :
    ∃ L : SimplicialObject.Truncated (FormalCoproduct.{max u v} (Over T)) (n + 1),
      (SimplicialObject.Truncated.trunc _ (n + 1) n).obj L = K ∧
        IsFiniteBasisTruncation J B T L
